title: Healthcare Social Workers
description: Provide individuals, families, and groups with the psychosocial support needed to cope with chronic, acute, or terminal illnesses. Services include advising family caregivers. Provide patients with information and counseling, and make referrals for other services. May also provide case and care management or interventions designed to promote health, prevent disease, and address barriers to access to healthcare.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Advocate for clients or patients to resolve crises.
Counsel clients and patients in individual and group sessions to help them overcome dependencies, recover from illness, and adjust to life.
Organize support groups or counsel family members to assist them in understanding, dealing with, and supporting the client or patient.
Develop or advise on social policy and assist in community development.
Utilize consultation data and social work experience to plan and coordinate client or patient care and rehabilitation, following through to ensure service efficacy.
Plan discharge from care facility to home or other care facility.
Modify treatment plans to comply with changes in clients' status.
Plan and conduct programs to combat social problems, prevent substance abuse, or improve community health and counseling services.
Investigate child abuse or neglect cases and take authorized protective action when necessary.
Identify environmental impediments to client or patient progress through interviews and review of patient records.
Conduct social research to advance knowledge in the social work field.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Educate clients about end-of-life symptoms and options to assist them in making informed decisions.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Collaborate with other professionals to evaluate patients' medical or physical condition and to assess client needs.

Refer patient, client, or family to community resources to assist in recovery from mental or physical illness and to provide access to services such as financial assistance, legal aid, housing, job placement or education.
Monitor, evaluate, and record client progress according to measurable goals described in treatment and care plan.
Supervise and direct other workers providing services to clients or patients.
Oversee Medicaid- and Medicare-related paperwork and recordkeeping in hospitals.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Video conferencing software
skills.def: Software to enable audio or video conferences between participants using networked devices. Examples: Google Meet, Zoom.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Microsoft Teams.

skills.name: Medical software
skills.def: Software to evaluate, plan, or redesign healthcare procedures. May include reporting or visualization features. Examples: Automated clinical information systems, Healthcare common procedure coding system HCPCS, James Frazier Associates DataStart, Medical procedure coding software.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Information presentation software, Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
